classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish individual balls in ordered draws with replacement, then count outcomes satisfying colour conditions.

content.prompt: A bag contains six balls: three red balls numbered 1 to 3, two white balls numbered 1 and 2, and one yellow ball. Two balls are selected one after the other, at random, and the first is replaced before the second is withdrawn.

answer.worked:
Let $R_1,R_2,R_3$ denote the red balls, $W_1,W_2$ the white balls and $Y$ the yellow ball. Record the draws as ordered pairs. Replacement allows every ball to appear on either draw, including the same ball twice. Listing the six possible second draws for each first draw gives:

$$\begin{aligned}\xi=\{&(R_1,R_1),(R_1,R_2),(R_1,R_3),(R_1,W_1),(R_1,W_2),(R_1,Y),\\&(R_2,R_1),(R_2,R_2),(R_2,R_3),(R_2,W_1),(R_2,W_2),(R_2,Y),\\&(R_3,R_1),(R_3,R_2),(R_3,R_3),(R_3,W_1),(R_3,W_2),(R_3,Y),\\&(W_1,R_1),(W_1,R_2),(W_1,R_3),(W_1,W_1),(W_1,W_2),(W_1,Y),\\&(W_2,R_1),(W_2,R_2),(W_2,R_3),(W_2,W_1),(W_2,W_2),(W_2,Y),\\&(Y,R_1),(Y,R_2),(Y,R_3),(Y,W_1),(Y,W_2),(Y,Y)\}.\end{aligned}$$

There are $6\times6=36$ equally likely outcomes.

children.label: i
children.prompt: both balls are the same colour

answer.worked:
Of the 36 equally likely ordered outcomes, 9 contain two red balls, 4 contain two white balls and 1 contains two yellow balls.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{same colour})&=\frac{9+4+1}{36}\\P(\text{same colour})&=\frac{14}{36}\\P(\text{same colour})&=\frac{7}{18}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: the two balls selected are different colours

answer.worked:
Count both orders for each pair of different colours: there are 12 red–white outcomes, 6 red–yellow outcomes and 4 white–yellow outcomes.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{different colours})&=\frac{12+6+4}{36}\\P(\text{different colours})&=\frac{22}{36}\\P(\text{different colours})&=\frac{11}{18}.\end{align*}$$
